results.title: JoyNews’ Emmanuel Adu Gyamfi wins GJA award for domestic tourism reporting
results.content: JoyNews’ Ahafo Regional Correspondent, Emmanuel Adu Gyamfi, has won the Best Reporter on Domestic Tourism award at the 30th Ghana Journalists Association (GJA) Media Awards. He was recognised for his article, “Speaking Ghana to the world: How indigenous languages can power tourism and economic growth,” at the awards ceremony held in Accra on Saturday, November 7, 2026. The Awards Committee, chaired by former Graphic Communications Group Editor Kobby Asmah, commended the report for demonstrating the value of development journalism and highlighting the role of Ghana’s indigenous languages in promoting tourism and economic growth. In its citation, the committee said the article drew attention to the potential of local languages as a tool for economic transformation.

results.title: Fifi Kwetey, Yameen, Ako Gunn go unopposed in NDC national executive race
results.content: The National Democratic Congress (NDC) has released the list of aspirants for its national executive elections scheduled for December 2026, with several key positions attracting no contest. The list, revealed on Monday, November 9, shows that four candidates are seeking the position of National Chairman, while Fifi Fiavi Kwetey, Joseph Yameen and Ako Gunn are going unopposed for their respective positions.

results.title: COP31: Africa makes progress on adoption of key supplementary priorities on agenda
results.content: COP31 must mark the definitive transition from negotiated promises to tangible financial delivery, the African Group of Negotiators (AGN) has urged world leaders in a decisive call as the 31st Conference of the Parties to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (COP31) opened in Antalya on Monday. Speaking on behalf of the continent at the opening plenary in Antalya, AGN Chair, Nana Dr. Antwi-Boasiako Amoah, emphasized that Africa’s ability to fulfill its climate commitments rests entirely on the immediate mobilization of scaled-up, predictable climate finance. Aligning the African block with the Group of 77 and China, Dr. Amoah declared that an implementation-focused summit must be a summit that delivers on finance, setting a firm tone for the two-week negotiations hosted by Türkiye with Australia presiding over negotiations.

results.title: Researchers urge government to fund Ghana-focused health studies and apply findings
results.content: Researchers and health professionals have called for increased government investment in local health research, warning that inadequate funding and the limited application of research findings could undermine efforts to address Ghana’s healthcare challenges. They say stronger support for indigenous research and closer collaboration between scientists, policymakers and healthcare practitioners are necessary to ensure evidence informs public policy and improves service delivery. The concerns were raised at the second Research Dissemination Day organised by HopeXchange Medical Centre, where experts also highlighted the challenges facing young researchers and the difficulties of translating scientific findings into practical interventions.

results.title: How Ghana can build an economy that produces more with her abundant resources
results.content: In September 2026, it took me more than twelve hours to travel the 266 kilometres from Nkroful to Kumasi through the important mining towns of Tarkwa, Bogosu, Dunkwa-on-Offin, Ayanfuri and Obuasi. In 2025, I compared Accra–Kumasi trips of at least six hours with a three-hour journey from Abidjan to Yamoussoukro over a similar distance. These were individual journeys, but they raise a question for every producer who depends on a road. How much of a working day can you afford to lose getting goods to market? The World Bank reported that Ghana’s economy grew by 6 per cent in 2025, yet only 13 per cent of workers aged 15 to 64 held formal wage or high-skilled jobs in 2023, down from 15 per cent in 2012. results.title: EOCO says visit to Wontumi’s property was for valuation, not a raid
results.content: The Economic and Organised Crime Office (EOCO) has denied reports that its officers ransacked a property belonging to the New Patriotic Party’s (NPP) Ashanti Regional Chairman, Bernard Antwi Boasiako, popularly known as Chairman Wontumi. In a statement issued on Monday, November 9, 2026, the Office said its officers, accompanied by officials from the Lands Commission, visited the Tema property to take coordinates and measurements for a professional valuation. EOCO said the exercise formed part of due process following the freezing of the property, which it said was confirmed by a court last year. “The said property was frozen by EOCO and confirmed by the Court last year. As part of due process, EOCO and Lands Commission officials were at the property to pick the coordinates and measurements to enable Lands Commission to conduct a professional valuation,” the statement said.

results.content: Ghana’s Ambassador to the United States, Victor Smith, has proposed compulsory military training for young people as part of efforts to promote discipline and address what he describes as growing indiscipline in the country. Speaking in an interview on JoyNews, Mr Smith suggested that young people leaving school should undergo military training for up to two years to instil discipline and keep them productively engaged. “Why don't we let the young people who come out of school do two years or so in military training? Just to sort of, if you like, put some discipline in people,” he said. The Ambassador argued that keeping young people engaged in structured activities could help address idleness, which he associated with corruption and other social problems. “The devil finds work for idle hands. results.title: Ghana in final talks with Boeing over revival of national airline – Victor Smith
results.content: Ghana’s Ambassador to the United States, Victor Smith, says negotiations with Boeing over the establishment of a national airline are nearing completion. Speaking in an interview on JoyNews, Mr Smith said the government was working to finalise arrangements to revive the national carrier, with efforts also underway to attract investors to the project. “We are looking for investors. They may invest in this effort. They may get something out of it. What is important for me is the legacy that the President will leave when he's leaving office—that we will have a national flag back in the air. That is important for me,” he said. Mr Smith said there was considerable public interest in the return of a national airline, arguing that many Ghanaians would welcome the opportunity to travel with a carrier bearing the country’s flag.

results.title: ‘Our young people are afraid of their shadows abroad’ – Ambassador Smith
results.content: Ghana’s Ambassador to the United States, Victor Smith, says some young Ghanaians living abroad are struggling with difficult conditions, including unemployment and fear, and has urged them to consider returning home with investors to create opportunities. He cited the Ghanaian community in Worcester, Massachusetts, where he estimates about 45,000 Ghanaians live, as an example of the challenges facing members of the diaspora. Speaking in a one-on-one interview with Desmond Danso on JoyNews, Ambassador Smith said some Ghanaians in the city were not working and appeared to live in fear. "I went to Worcester in Massachusetts and there are about 45,000 Ghanaians in Worcester alone. And ask me whether they are working. No. They're not. And they are even afraid of their shadows that the eyes will pick them. So, they are spending most of their time in their churches," he said.

results.title: Ghana Ambassador to US Victor Smith urges diaspora to attract investment and create jobs
results.content: Ghana's Ambassador to the United States, Victor Smith, has urged the Ghanaian diaspora to return home with investors to create jobs and opportunities for young people. Speaking in a one-on-one interview with Desmond Danso on JoyNews, Ambassador Smith said he is actively engaging investors in the US to sell the opportunities that exist in Ghana. "Now, that is where I am on the other side of the Atlantic asking us to sell the opportunities that exist to the foreign investors. There are big opportunities in mining, energy, agriculture, you name it, manufacturing," he stated.
